A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same A0 research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original waypoint-prediction experiments, architecture ablations, real-robot success rates, and qualitative demonstrations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports expanded VLA comparisons and additional demonstrations using high-level planning.

M1.justification: Appendix B.2 and Figure 8 explicitly introduce VLM-based task decomposition for stage-by-stage execution by A0. This extends the existing use of a VLM for waypoint-height selection; the diffusion architecture, losses, affordance representation, and basic action-execution procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The four source datasets and four standard robot tasks remain. Figure 8 adds multi-object fruit placement and flower-insertion demonstrations using high-level planning. DROID-2k becoming DROID-3k reflects an increased sample count within retained coverage, rather than a new dataset domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds the existing RDT-1B baseline, labeled RDT, to the Kinova comparison alongside MOKA and ReKep. RDT-1B, π0, and π0 + FAST already appear in v1 Table 3, and the RoboPoint comparison already appears in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Section 5.1.1 changes the reported pretraining budget from 200 epochs to 80,000 steps and fine-tuning from 40,000 to 30,000 steps. The DROID subset increases from 2,000 to 3,056 trajectories while retaining the 80:20 split. Section 5.2.3 extends five-episode VLA fine-tuning from Wipe Board to each of four tasks. These are substantial reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The pretraining and component ablations, along with the appendix background-generalization examples, are retained. New Figure 8 provides qualitative case studies of whether VLM planning enables more complex manipulation. No quantitative planner ablation or additional robustness analysis accompanies these demonstrations.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 trials per standard real-robot task and present point estimates. Neither adds seed information, uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or a changed statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes Wipe Board success rates from 10, 35, and 30 to 0, 10, and 0 for RDT-1B, π0, and π0 + FAST, respectively; A0 remains at 50. It also adds results for three other tasks and task averages. Previously reported Table 2 rows, Table 1 ablation values, and Table 4 RoboPoint results remain numerically unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the revised wiping baseline scores, so the larger margin does not establish improved A0 performance across versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same representation definitions, diffusion mathematics, losses, projection, grasp selection, and MAE definition. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and principal contributions retain their original claims. The conclusion adds that VLM decomposition enables stage-by-stage execution for long-horizon and orientation-sensitive tasks, modestly extending the stated applicability.

C2.justification: v1 discusses grasp-sampler generalization and depth/occlusion limitations. v4 retains these and adds substantive discussion of orientation-sensitive control and long-horizon planning, including viewpoint selection, track-guided control, and VLM decomposition as possible mitigations.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses four A100 80GB GPUs, batch size 200, memory consumption of 73GB per GPU, and pretraining/fine-tuning durations of five days and 50 hours. The annotation pipeline, project link, and prospective dataset-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The main related-work survey and 60 referenced works are retained. Appendix B.2 adds connections to ATM's track-guided control and discusses long-horizon planning relative to MOKA, ReKep, and π0.5. ATM's updated bibliography entry represents the same work, not a newly added citation.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in experimental settings, the VLA-results paragraph, the conclusion, and new Appendix B.2; Future Work moves to B.3. There are also affiliation and punctuation edits. The overall narrative remains intact, although v4 introduces an unresolved ATM citation and incorrectly redirects Section 5.2.4 to Figure 8.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands into a full-width, four-task display, and Table 2 gains an RDT row. Figure 8 is new; v1 Figures 8–11 become Figures 9–12, with appendix and reference reflow. Table 3 introduces swapped Steps and Avg. Success headings while retaining a caption describing only Wipe Board.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens the empirical account by comparing VLA baselines across all four standard tasks, disclosing resource requirements, and clarifying important applicability limits. The planning demonstrations add useful qualitative evidence. These benefits are tempered by unexplained wiping-baseline revisions, swapped Table 3 headings, and an incorrect figure reference; the new planning capability also lacks quantitative validation.
